answer: Cross-epoch trajectory matching. Each identity's action sequence is hashed into an order-sensitive cipher chain, and a validator recomputes the chain over the prior epoch, projecting it forward on a spiral of expected drift. An identity whose new epoch diverges beyond tolerance is throttled to low-value lanes at a wharf-like staging queue until it re-earns continuity. Attackers must maintain consistent, costly behaviour across every epoch for each clone, multiplying their operating burden per identity.
